runConfig.positivePrompt: Scientific educational image-to-video for ages five to fourteen. Static locked wide camera, one continuous forward-only five-second shot with no cuts. Preserve the attached approved still as the exact first-frame identity, anatomy, left-facing full-body composition, lighting, palette, skin markings, terrain, vegetation, and crop reference. Exactly one complete Giganotosaurus carolinii remains in frame with one long low rectangular skull, a narrow snout tip, one low swept-back lacrimal ridge, two short three-fingered forelimbs, exactly two strong hind limbs with two planted three-toed feet, and one complete continuous balancing tail. After a brief opening hold, the dinosaur itself makes one clearly visible attentive motion: the complete skull, muscular neck, throat, shoulder base, and upper chest lift together smoothly by seven to nine degrees and move slightly forward, with natural connected tissue and no isolated head hinge. The closed jaws and skull proportions remain constant. The final second holds the new higher attentive pose. Keep the torso, pelvis, both forelimbs, both planted hind feet, toes, and the entire tail stable at their source coordinates. Keep all trees, plants, clouds, shadows, and ground completely still. No return, reverse, second nod, repeated motion, walk, or loop.
